 How to follow Mexico City Grand Prix on the BBC 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The Mexico City Grand Prix signed a contract extension last year to stay on the F1 calendar until 2028
 By Sophie Trifonoff BBC Sport journalist Published 26 October 2026 
 Updated 29 October 2026 Round 19 of the 2026 Formula 1 season heads to the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez for the Mexico City Grand Prix, from 30 October to 1 November. 
 Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli sealed victory from pole position last time out in the United States, and was joined on the podium by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
 The 20-year-old Italian is now 123 points clear of team-mate George Russell in the drivers' standings, and will make history in Mexico as the youngest F1 world champion if he finishes ninth or better.
 If Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not win the race, Antonelli will lift the title wherever he finishes.
 Lights out for Sunday's 71-lap race is at 20:00 GMT.

 Session start times and BBC coverage 
 Commentary of the weekend will be available across BBC Radio 5 Live, 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app.
 You can also ask your smart speaker to "play 5 Live", for example.
 Make sure to listen to every episode of the Chequered Flag podcast. For the first time this year, the post-race show for every grand prix is available to watch on BBC iPlayer and YouTube. , external 
 All times GMT 
 Friday, 30 October 
 First practice: 18:30-19:30 - 5 Sports Extra 
 Second practice: 22:00-23:00 - 5 Sports Extra 
 Saturday, 31 October 
 Third practice: 17:30-18:30 - 5 Sports Extra 
 Qualifying: 21:00-22:00 - 5 Sports Extra 
 Sunday, 1 November 
 Race: 20:00 - 5 Live 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, World champion Lando Norris took a dominant win in Mexico City last year, with Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen also on the podium
 What is the Mexico City weather forecast? 
 The forecast suggests it will be a warm weekend in the Mexican capital, but Friday's practice sessions could see some light rain. 
 For Sunday's race, which starts at 2pm local time, conditions should be dry with a high temperatures of 24C.
